strings.name: Safra Catz
strings.role: Oracle executive vice chair and former CEO
strings.summary: Catz brought investment banking, finance and acquisition experience to Oracle’s expansion, serving as president, CFO and CEO. In September 2025 she handed CEO duties to Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia and became executive vice chair, continuing work on direction and governance.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: She contributed to Oracle’s acquisitions, finance and enterprise software management, influencing database industry consolidation and cloud computing development.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Wharton undergraduate degree, University of Pennsylvania, 1983; J.D., Penn Law, 1986.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Connecting transactions and operations
strings.highlights.h1.text: At Oracle she helped shape acquisition strategy, financial management and operating integration, applying banking experience to enterprise software management.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Cloud transition and succession
strings.highlights.h2.text: As CEO she participated in cloud expansion before becoming executive vice chair; product development and engineering also depended on other leaders and teams.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Becoming executive vice chair
strings.timeline.t1.text: Her CEO tenure ended as Magouyrk and Sicilia became joint CEOs; she continued board and strategic work in the new role.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Becoming sole CEO
strings.timeline.t2.text: Following co-CEO Mark Hurd’s death, she held the role alone and continued leading business operations.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Appointment as co-CEO
strings.timeline.t3.text: As Larry Ellison moved to executive chair and technology duties, she and Hurd shared the chief executive position.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Returning as CFO
strings.timeline.t4.text: She again became CFO while remaining president, continuing finance and operational responsibilities until the 2014 leadership changes.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becoming Oracle president
strings.timeline.t5.text: She entered the company’s highest operational leadership and later also served several periods as CFO.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining the board
strings.timeline.t6.text: She became an Oracle director, connecting management responsibilities with board governance.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joining Oracle
strings.timeline.t7.text: She left investment banking at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette for management in enterprise software.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Law degree and investment banking
strings.timeline.t8.text: After earning her Penn J.D., she began an investment banking career and later became a managing director.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Completing Wharton studies
strings.timeline.t9.text: She earned an undergraduate business degree before studying law, building combined financial and legal training.
